bull.b: AMVUTTRA’s rapid uptake and broad TTR expansion demonstrate strong commercial execution and growing adoption in a defined rare-disease franchise. Continued prescriber additions and high adherence can support durable product revenue over the next several quarters.

Strong operating and free cash flow indicate that Alnylam’s recent profitability is translating into usable cash rather than relying solely on accounting earnings. This supports continued investment in clinical programs, commercial expansion, and balance-sheet strengthening.

Multiple clinical programs across development stages provide opportunities to broaden the platform beyond current products and reduce reliance on one franchise over time. Upcoming data readouts and continued IND filings create a pipeline for future product and revenue growth.

bear.b: The TTR guidance reduction shows that initial launch dynamics were stronger than the sustainable near-term demand trajectory. Although the revised range still implies substantial growth, normalization raises execution risk and makes future revenue expansion more dependent on new patient starts.

Higher royalty rates transfer more of the product economics to partners as AMVUTTRA revenue grows, limiting operating leverage from commercial scale. Persistent royalty pressure could constrain margin expansion and reduce the cash contribution of future product growth.

Rapidly rising R&D and SG&A spending increases the investment required to sustain pipeline progress and commercial expansion. If revenue growth moderates or programs take longer to mature, elevated costs could pressure margins and make the recent profit improvement less durable.
